production.note: Calendar years of customer deliveries; the car was never sold in the US, so the record uses the German home market. Top Gear (Ollie Marriage): "the first of the 275 customers receiving their £2.3m toys in autumn 2022 and the last by the end of 2023." Limited to 275 cars (classiccars-journal-amg-one).

body.note: Two-seat fixed-roof hypercar; inferred from the review.

displacementL.note: 1,599 cc. Mercedes-Benz press release technical data: "Displacement | 1599 cc".

fuel.note: Mercedes-AMG: an "E PERFORMANCE plug-in hybrid" system.

drivetrain.note: Quote (Mercedes-Benz press release): "It features the AMG Performance 4MATIC+ fully variable all-wheel drive with hybrid-driven rear axle and electrically driven front axle with torque vectoring."

transmission.note: "7-speed automated manual gearbox" (Mercedes-AMG site: "automated 7-speed manual transmission").

powerHp.note: Combined system output. Quote (Mercedes-Benz press release technical data, reproduced by Auto International): "Max. system output | 782 kW (1063 hp)" (the "hp" is PS). 782 kW x 1.34102 = 1,049 hp (1,063 PS x 0.98632 = 1,048 hp). Mercedes-AMG site: "782/1,063 kW/hp" (mercedes-amg-one-site). Top Gear: "Peak combined power is a claimed 1,049bhp" (topgear-amg-one).

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: a single named-author article (prose, not a spec panel, and not labelled kerb or dry) with a database agreeing. Quote (Top Gear, Ollie Marriage): "Given that the One weighs a bloated 1,695kg, it's within the clutches of a lot of less expensive cars, not least Ferrari's ballistic SF90 Stradale." autotijd.be (database): "Kerb (curb) weight DIN | 1,695 kg" (autotijd-amg-one). 1,695 kg x 2.20462 = 3,737 lb. Uncounted corroboration: ClassicCars.com Journal prints a technical-data table with "Kerb weight according to DIN | kg | 1695" but without byline or attribution (classiccars-journal-amg-one). Single configuration.

sources.publisher: Mercedes-Benz (press release reproduced by Auto International, "From Mercedes-Benz Press Release")

provisionalNote: Weight is provisional: 1,695 kg (3,737 lb) rests on Top Gear's review prose (Ollie Marriage, one named-author article, figure not labelled kerb or dry), with autotijd.be (database) agreeing that it is a DIN kerb weight; an unattributed ClassicCars.com Journal table also shows it but is not counted. The Mercedes-Benz press release technical data with the weight row (Mercedes media site), or an Evo, Autocar or Top Gear specification panel, would replace it. Power is from the Mercedes-Benz press release.
